page: Amazon Web Services r7a.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine managed by the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9R14 processor configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs (1 thread per core). Memory capacity is 64.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per core. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, contains no dedicated local NVMe storage, and includes no hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark testing demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2076.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3075.89, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. It also shows elevated performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 13.93 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation at 304.57 tokens/sec. Multithreaded operations align with average expectations for an 8-core slice, reflecting a Geekbench multi-core score of 10685.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 20038.21. In memory-intensive testing, cached small-block reads reach 1184.87 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to 38.35 GB/sec, ranking in the lower quartile.

With its 8:1 memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, the r7a.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for memory-bound applications without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading (SMT). Because it lacks local storage, workloads must rely on network-attached storage architectures. The system is well fitted for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput data processing, and enterprise application backends requiring stable single-core frequency and substantial DDR5 memory headroom.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the Nitro hypervisor, equipped with an 8-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration allocates 1 thread per core without SMT, includes 32 MB of L3 cache, and provides 3 Gbps of baseline networking. It contains no local storage volumes and no GPU accelerators. Performance metrics show top-quartile single-core throughput, including a 2076.0 Geekbench single-core result, alongside steady multi-core compute and caching capabilities like 19.78 million Redis SET operations per second. However, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth remains in the lower quartile. This setup suits memory-intensive enterprise tasks, in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and data processing pipelines.
